lyrics:
[Intro: low piano chords, a hummed choir note]

[Verse 1: soulful, low, piano and voice]
She laughs like a gavel coming down
She rules against my sorrow and she throws my worries out
I was guilty of the usual, the hiding and the doubt
She read me like a sentence and she let me out

[Pre-Chorus: organ enters, choir hums]
I've stood in rooms where they told me who to be
Hand on a book that was never about me

[Chorus: full choir, heavy drums, voice soars]
Swear me in
I'll tell the whole truth with my hands up
Swear me in
I'll take the stand and I'll stand up
Raise my right hand to your left
I do, I do, I do
Swear me in

[Verse 2: soulful, fuller, bass and tambourine]
If I'm a witness, let me testify at night
The only law I answer to is whether we're alright
They can keep their robes and benches and their Sunday best
I have seen the evidence, and I can rest

[Pre-Chorus: organ and choir rising]
I've stood in rooms where they told me who to be
Hand on a book that was never about me

[Chorus: full choir, heavy drums, voice soars]
Swear me in
I'll tell the whole truth with my hands up
Swear me in
I'll take the stand and I'll stand up
Raise my right hand to your left
I do, I do, I do
Swear me in

[Bridge: drums drop out, voice and handclaps, choir answers]
When the door is closed there's nobody to rule
(Nobody, nobody)
Only what we promised, only me and you
(Only me and you)
So help me

[Final Chorus: loudest, choir at full voice, melisma on the last line]
Swear me in
I'll tell the whole truth with my hands up
Swear me in
I'll take the stand and I'll stand up
Raise my right hand to your left
I do, I do, I do
Swear me in

[Outro: choir alone, one piano chord]
I do
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 64 BPM, a slow, heavy sway in 4/4 with a dragging triplet lilt. E minor. Solemn, bluesy and enormous.

VOICE: Male, a warm baritone with a tenor's top, soulful and slightly rough, with an Irish colour to the vowels. Low and intimate in the verses, full-throated in the chorus. The phrase 'I do' is stretched across a long run of notes. A mixed gospel choir sings behind him and alone at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: A dark, simple piano. Church organ. A gospel choir. Heavy, slow drums with a deep kick and a cracking snare. Electric bass. Handclaps and tambourine. A gritty electric guitar playing blues fills. Low strings.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and a hummed note. 0:15 Verse 1. 0:45 Pre-chorus, organ and choir. 1:00 Chorus 1, drums and full choir. 1:30 Verse 2. 2:00 Pre-chorus. 2:15 Chorus 2. 2:45 Bridge, drums out, voice with handclaps and choir answers. 3:07 Final chorus at full strength. 3:37 Outro, the choir alone on two words and a last piano chord at 3:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2010s indie soul: raw and roomy, as if recorded in a stone hall, the voice close and the choir far and wide.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The run of notes on 'I do' at the end of the first chorus.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man's argument with an institution. This is a settled love speaking, and the oath is one he chooses. It can be sung at a wedding without irony.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Relief, defiance, a vow.
